method: Ideal horizontal centre-range only, one-unit midpoint bins; shared-preview gun/Arc48/72, physically surveyed gun96 and silo72/96/120. Play-only ranges and active tier2 profiles differ. Separate production geometry/LOS/pitch/contact/flight reports govern selected designs. Each plot is an independent alternative; overlapping route intervals are not additive damage.

options.title: Tarn and Fir Circuit
options.rationale: Tours northern fir ground, the eastern tarn bank and a southern return. Keeps both raised slate islands and the whole lake intact; north/early, long eastern contact and late southern alternatives remain separated.

options.title: Western Tarn Fold
options.rationale: A northern approach visits western ground before a lower-bank return. Avoids the long eastern transit and costs less eastern scenery, but leaves the substantial east bank scenic and clusters more opportunities west of the tarn.

options.title: Meltwater Crossing and Return
options.rationale: A short northern approach crosses the original meltwater on two wooden deck boxes, then folds through a broad western court and returns below the southern ridge. Bridge-bank investment, western return coverage and a separate southeast catch make different choices.

options.title: Upper Bend Tour
options.rationale: Crosses from southwestern ground and tours the northern bank before a northeast exit. Northern courts gain a larger role, but the entire southern ridge and much lower ground cease to contribute to defence choice.

options.title: White Ridge Confluence
options.rationale: A long western fold crosses the stream once and meets a distinct northern-bank approach. Shared eastern-corridor coverage leads to a southern catch, preserving the ridge as a backdrop and offering western-only, northern-only and common-tail investments.

options.title: Western Ridge Fold
options.rationale: A completely dry western fold avoids a stream crossing and keeps all eastern ridge scenery intact. Several western returns are useful, but the eastern bank never enters play and it offers no distinct branch investment.

options.title: Sanctuary and Mere Fold
options.rationale: Passes through the clear corridor between the raised sanctuary fragments, returns beside the northern mere shore, then descends east of the western ridge to a separate southern catch. The large southeastern lake stays uninterrupted; two broad internal courts support different contact times.

options.title: Sanctuary Shore Crossing
options.rationale: The northern entry visits the eastern sanctuary and briefly bridges the lake lip before returning through central and western courts. It uses more eastern scenery and has a more elaborate late fold; the lake crossing adds engineering/scenic cost without creating a stronger independent final catch.
